description: Charging gaps on highways: "charging gaps on I-80", "where can't I fast charge on I-90 in Montana?". Stretches over 50 miles of U.S. Interstates, U.S. highways and designated EV Alternative Fuel Corridors with no fast charger within 5 miles of the highway, measured in a straight line (measure "practical", the default, longest first). With measure "nevi": stretches with no fast charger within 1 mile of the highway (the federal NEVI siting distance), by state and highway, each listing the fast chargers 1 to 5 miles off with name, city, network, fast ports, plugs, miles off and nearest mile marker. Filter by state, highway and length. From our daily open-data files (CC BY 4.0); each answer carries the file's version, date, definition and cite_as line.

designated.description: true: only gaps on FHWA-designated Alternative Fuel Corridors; false: only undesignated ones

highway.description: Highway as signed, e.g. I-70, US-40, CO-82

measure.description: practical: no fast charger within 5 miles of the highway, measured in a straight line (the headline measure). nevi: no fast charger within 1 mile of the highway (the federal NEVI siting distance), with the chargers 1 to 5 miles off each stretch.

min_miles.description: Only gaps at least this long, in miles

name: get_charging_gaps
title: Highway charging gaps
